result.notes:

FIX 1 (PolkitPolicyIntegrityTests.cs): line 28-29 now `ISystemServices services = SystemServicesBuilder.Real().Build();` then `string policyPath = Path.Combine(services.Environment.GetBaseDirectory(), "agentguard-presence.policy");`; deleted the RepoRoot() helper and `using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;`; updated the class doc to the base-directory mechanism. Removing [CallerFilePath] clears the AG0039 ban, intended.

FIX 2 (BaseDirectorySeparatorTests.cs): added standalone fact FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededAlreadyTerminated_ReturnsItUnchangedWithExactlyOneSeparator — seed FakeEnvironment.Create(seed, baseDirectory: seed + separator), assert .Be(seed + separator) exact equality. Kept as a documented standalone guard (not folded into a Theory) so the three existing facts stay as-is. Per the fix note it is green now against the passthrough fake (regression guard for the append feature); the RED forcing function for the separator logic is the un-terminated sibling fact.

FIX 3 (BaseDirectorySeparatorTests.cs, DRY): hoisted real.Platform.FileSystem.DirectorySeparator into a single readonly `separator` field beside `real`, initialized in a constructor (field initializers run before the ctor body, so `real` is available; a field initializer cannot reference `real` directly — CS0236 — hence the ctor). Removed the per-method local and referenced the field in all four facts.

Real-adapter facts (accessor + RealBaseDirectory + the Linux polkit test) go RED because EnvironmentAdapter.GetBaseDirectory() throws NotSupportedException (ARCHITECTURE skeleton stub, EnvironmentAdapter.cs:49). The fake facts go RED because FakeEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory() is a passthrough (=> _baseDirectory) with no separator logic yet: un-terminated seed returns "/Users/timothystockstill" not ".../", and the Fake() default (Host.Home = real home, no trailing separator) is unterminated too.

Its RED is the same NotSupportedException throw from EnvironmentAdapter.GetBaseDirectory() and is proven only on the Linux CI leg — stated plainly per the contract's Acceptance #3 note.

The modified src/AgentGuard.Abstractions/Contracts/IEnvironment.cs, src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/EnvironmentAdapter.cs, and tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/FakeEnvironment.cs shown in git status are the pre-existing ARCHITECTURE skeleton (frozen to me); I did not touch them. findings.summary: The `seed` setup value is copy-pasted verbatim across two Fact methods in BaseDirectorySeparatorTests instead of being hoisted the way the same class already hoists `real` and `separator`.
findings.evidence: tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/BaseDirectorySeparatorTests.cs:50 and :66 — both lines read the identical `string seed = real.Environment.GetHomeDirectory().TrimEnd(separator);`. The surrounding blocks repeat further: lines 52-56 (`FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededWithoutATrailingSeparator_AppendsExactlyOne`) and lines 68-72 (`FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededAlreadyTerminated_ReturnsItUnchangedWithExactlyOneSeparator`) both do `IEnvironment fake = FakeEnvironment.Create(seed, baseDirectory: <input>);` then `fake.GetBaseDirectory().Should().Be(seed + separator, "...")` — same logic, differing only in the `baseDirectory:` argument (`seed` vs `seed + separator`) and the assertion message string. The class's own constructor (lines 28-33) already establishes the correct pattern — computing `real` and `separator` once and sharing them across all four facts — so this is an inconsistent, not-yet-applied instance of that same practice, not an isolated one-off.
findings.fix: Hoist the seed into a private readonly field computed once in the constructor, mirroring `separator`: `private readonly string seed;` set via `seed = real.Environment.GetHomeDirectory().TrimEnd(separator);` right after `separator` is assigned, then reference `seed` at lines 52/54-55 and 68/70-71 instead of recomputing it. Stronger alternative: collapse the two Facts into one `[Theory]` with `[InlineData(false)]`/`[InlineData(true)]` over `alreadyTerminated`, building `string seedInput = alreadyTerminated ? seed + separator : seed;` and sharing the single `Create(...)` + `Should().Be(seed + separator, ...)` block — this removes the duplicated block entirely rather than just the duplicated line.

findings.evidence: tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/BaseDirectorySeparatorTests.cs:59-73. Verified by actually running `dotnet test tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~BaseDirectorySeparatorTests`: result is 3 Failed, 1 Passed, and the xUnit trace names the other three facts explicitly as [FAIL] (RealBaseDirectory_EndsWithADirectorySeparator, FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededWithoutATrailingSeparator_AppendsExactlyOne, FakeBaseDirectory_OnTheDefaultHomeFallbackPath_EndsWithADirectorySeparator) — leaving FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededAlreadyTerminated_ReturnsItUnchangedWithExactlyOneSeparator as the one that passed. Root cause: tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/FakeEnvironment.cs:108 today is `public string GetBaseDirectory() => _baseDirectory;` — a bare field return with none of Decision 5's 'test for trailing separator, append when absent' logic. The test seeds `baseDirectory: seed + separator` (already terminated), so the naive passthrough already returns `seed + separator` unmodified, coincidentally matching the assertion with zero of the required logic written. This is the exact Rail #2 pattern: 'for an expansion, the CURRENT wrong behavior' happens to equal the correct behavior for this one input, so the test 'can never catch whether the change was made.'

Do not leave it silently green.

findings.summary: Acceptance test FakeBaseDirectory_WhenSeededAlreadyTerminated_ReturnsItUnchangedWithExactlyOneSeparator is GREEN before implementation, violating rails-test-code rail 2 (RED before green): its own gate asks 'none green before implementation?' and the answer here is no. It seeds the fake with an already-separator-terminated value and asserts the value returns unchanged, but the current skeleton FakeEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory() => _baseDirectory returns the raw field, which for an already-terminated seed already equals the expected output — so the test passes today and cannot catch whether the Decision-5 normalization is ever implemented. It is the legitimately-required two-sided (no-double) guard, so it must exist; it is green only because the fake skeleton returns the raw field instead of throwing. Every OTHER acceptance test in the suite is correctly RED (the real adapter throws NotSupportedException; the append-side and default-fallback fake tests fail on the expected-vs-actual separator).
